triples.rationale: Azariah's prayer blesses the God of the fathers and His enduring name. The later communal hymn opens with that same blessing of the fathers' God and His name.
triples.source_text: “Blessed art Thou, Lord, God of our fathers; Thy name is praised and glorified for ever.

target_units.text: “Blessed art Thou, Lord, God of our fathers, praised and highly exalted for ever. Blessed is the holy name of Thy glory, exceedingly praised and highly exalted through all ages.

triples.rationale: Azariah confesses that God's deeds and judgments are righteous. Daniel's later prayer likewise calls God righteous in the calamities brought upon a people who did not obey His voice.
triples.source_text: For Thou art righteous in everything Thou hast done to us; all Thy works are true, Thy ways upright, and all Thy judgments true.

target_units.text: The Lord God kept watch over the calamities and brought them upon us, for the Lord our God is righteous in everything He may do, and we did not listen to His voice.

triples.rationale: The prayer attributes Jerusalem's judgment to the people's sins. Daniel later appeals for wrath to turn from Jerusalem while confessing that the people's sins made the city and people a reproach.
triples.source_text: Thou hast carried out judgments of truth in everything Thou didst bring upon us and upon Thy holy city, our fathers’ Jerusalem. For in truth and judgment Thou didst all these things because of our sins.

target_units.text: Master, according to Thy righteousness, let Thy wrath and anger turn away from Thy city Jerusalem, Thy holy mountain. Because of our sins and our fathers’ acts of ignorance, Jerusalem and Thy people, Lord, are a reproach among all around us.

triples.rationale: Both prayers confess collective sin, lawless conduct and departure from God's commands, placing the speakers within the people's wrongdoing rather than treating them as detached observers.
triples.source_text: For we have sinned in everything and acted lawlessly by departing from Thee. We have sinned in everything and have not obeyed the commands of Thy law.

target_units.text: we have sinned, done wrong, acted impiously, fallen away, and transgressed Thy commandments and judgments,

triples.rationale: Azariah says the people failed to keep the commands given for their good; Daniel's later confession says Israel refused God's voice and abandoned the law, bringing its curse upon them.
triples.source_text: We have neither kept nor done what Thou didst command us, so that it might go well with us.

target_units.text: and have not listened to the voice of the Lord our God, to follow Thy law that Thou didst set before Moses and us through Thy servants the prophets.
All Israel abandoned Thy law and fell away, refusing to hear Thy voice. The curse and oath written in the law of Moses, God’s servant, came upon us, because we sinned against Him.

triples.rationale: The prayer calls the judgments brought upon the people true. Daniel's later prayer similarly says the announced calamities came according to the covenant and affirms God's righteousness in them.
triples.source_text: And now, everything Thou hast brought upon us and everything Thou hast done to us, Thou hast done in true judgment.

target_units.text: He established for us His commands, all He spoke against us and against our judges, all Thou didst judge for us, bringing great calamities upon us, such as had not occurred under heaven as occurred in Jerusalem.

According to what is written in Moses’ covenant, all the calamities came upon us. Yet we did not seek the face of the Lord our God by departing from our sins and understanding Thy righteousness, Lord.
The Lord God kept watch over the calamities and brought them upon us, for the Lord our God is righteous in everything He may do, and we did not listen to His voice.

triples.rationale: Azariah describes being handed over to hostile enemies and an unjust king. Chronicles likewise describes God handing the people into Chaldean power, followed by destruction and captivity; the shared connection is the judgment of exile.
triples.source_text: Thou didst hand us over to our enemies, lawless and most hateful apostates, and to an unjust king, the most wicked in all the earth.

target_units.text: He brought against them a king of the Chaldeans, who killed their young men with the sword in the house of his sanctuary and did not spare Zedekiah. They had no mercy on their virgins and carried away their elders. He handed everything into their hands.
All the vessels of God’s house, great and small, the treasures, and all the treasures of the king and the magnates—he brought everything into Babylon.
He burned the Lord’s house, demolished Jerusalem’s wall, and burned its citadels with fire, consigning every beautiful article to destruction.
He deported the survivors to Babylon, and they became slaves to him and his sons until the kingdom of the Medes,

triples.rationale: The prayer says the speakers cannot open their mouths because shame and reproach have come upon them. Daniel's later prayer similarly contrasts God's righteousness with the shame of Judah, Jerusalem, Israel and their rulers because of sin.
triples.source_text: Now we cannot open our mouths; shame and reproach have come upon Thy servants and those who revere Thee.

target_units.text: Righteousness belongs to Thee, Lord, but shame of face to us as on this day—to the people of Judah, those dwelling in Jerusalem, and all the people Israel, near and far, in all the countries where Thou didst scatter them because of the trespass they committed before Thee.
Master, shame of face belongs to us, to our kings, rulers, and fathers, because we have sinned against Thee.

triples.rationale: The prayer asks God not to hand the people over utterly or dissolve the covenant. In Leviticus God says He did not disregard them in enemy territory so as to consume them or dissolve His covenant, and that He will remember it. The petition appeals to that covenant fidelity.
triples.source_text: Do not hand us over utterly, for Thy name’s sake; do not dissolve Thy covenant.

target_units.text: And yet even so, while they were in their enemies’ land, I did not disregard them or become indignant with them so as to consume them and dissolve My covenant with them, for I am the Lord their God.
And I will remember for them the former covenant, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of a house of slavery, before the nations to be their God. I am the Lord.

triples.rationale: Azariah appeals for the sake of Abraham, Isaac and Israel. Exodus describes God hearing Israel's groaning and remembering His covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the same patriarchal covenant invoked for help.
triples.source_text: Do not remove Thy mercy from us, for the sake of Abraham, beloved by Thee, and Isaac Thy servant, and Israel Thy holy one,

target_units.text: God heard their groaning, and God remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

triples.rationale: The prayer recalls the promise of descendants like heaven's stars and the seashore's sand. Genesis records those two images together in the promise to Abraham.
triples.source_text: as Thou didst speak to them, saying that Thou wouldst multiply their descendants like the stars of heaven and the sand along the shore of the sea.

target_units.text: surely I will bless you, and greatly multiply your seed as the stars of the heaven, and as the sand upon the shore of the sea; and your seed shall inherit the cities of their adversaries.

triples.rationale: The people lament their diminished numbers and low condition because of sins. Deuteronomy warns that disobedience will leave them few after being as numerous as heaven's stars, matching the prayer's contrast with the preceding promise.
triples.source_text: For, Master, we have been diminished beyond all nations, and today we are lowly throughout the earth because of our sins.

target_units.text: And you shall be left few in number, whereas you were as the stars of heaven in multitude, because you did not hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God.

triples.relationship: shared deprivation of rule and worship
triples.rationale: The prayer laments the lack of rulers and sacrificial worship. Hosea likewise describes Israel remaining without king, ruler, sacrifice, altar and priesthood; the connection is the stated deprivation, without equating the passages' dates.
triples.source_text: At this time there is no ruler or prophet or leader, no burnt offering or sacrifice or offering or incense, no place to offer produce before Thee and find mercy.

target_units.text: For Israel’s sons will remain many days without king or ruler, without sacrifice or altar, without priesthood or manifestations.

triples.rationale: Azariah asks that a crushed soul and humbled spirit be accepted as with burnt offerings. The psalm likewise contrasts burnt offerings with the broken spirit and humbled heart that God does not despise, bringing inward humility into the language of acceptable sacrifice.
triples.source_text: But with a crushed soul and humbled spirit may we be accepted, as with burnt offerings of rams and bulls, and as with tens of thousands of fat lambs.

target_units.text: For if Thou hadst desired sacrifice, I would have given it; Thou wilt not delight in burnt offerings.
A sacrifice to God is a broken spirit; a broken and humbled heart God will not despise.

triples.rationale: The prayer's explicit trust clause affirms that those who trust God will not be put to shame. The psalm similarly joins trust in God with freedom from shame. This connection does not interpret the source's separate quoted 'behind Thee' phrases.
triples.source_text: So may our sacrifice be before Thee today; and be propitious—“behind Thee”; for there is no shame for those who trust in Thee; and bring to completion—“behind Thee.”

target_units.text: In Thee I have trusted; may I not be put to shame, and let my enemies not laugh at me.
For indeed, all who wait for Thee will certainly not be put to shame; let all who act lawlessly without cause be ashamed.

triples.rationale: The companions turn to God with their whole heart and seek His face. Deuteronomy describes seeking God with the whole heart in distress among the nations and finding His covenant mercy.
triples.source_text: Now we follow with our whole heart; we fear Thee and seek Thy face. Do not put us to shame,

target_units.text: And there you shall seek the Lord your God, and shall find Him, when you seek Him with all your heart and with all your soul, in your distress.
And all these things shall find you in the latter days, and you shall return unto the Lord your God, and hearken unto His voice.
For the Lord your God is a merciful God; He will not forsake you, neither will He destroy you, nor forget the covenant of your fathers which He sware unto them.

triples.rationale: The plea asks God to act with gentleness and mercy toward the shamed petitioners. Daniel's later prayer expressly rests its supplication on God's mercy rather than the petitioners' righteous deeds.
triples.source_text: but deal with us according to Thy gentleness and the abundance of Thy mercy.

target_units.text: Attend with Thine ear, Lord, and hear me. Open Thine eyes and see our desolation and that of Thy city, over which Thy name has been called. For we make our supplication in our prayers before Thee because of Thy mercy, not our righteous deeds.

triples.rationale: Azariah asks for rescue and glory for God's name. The psalm likewise asks the Savior to rescue and forgive for the glory of His name, joining deliverance with the honor of that name.
triples.source_text: Rescue us according to Thy wondrous deeds, and give glory to Thy name, Lord.

target_units.text: Help us, God our Savior. For the glory of Thy name, Lord, rescue us, and be propitious toward our sins for Thy name’s sake,

triples.rationale: The prayer asks for the shame and humiliation of those who harm God's servants. The psalm likewise asks for the enemies' faces to be dishonored and for them to be ashamed and troubled.
triples.source_text: May all who inflict evil on Thy servants be ashamed; may they be humiliated out of all their power, and may their strength be crushed.

target_units.text: Fill their faces with dishonor, and they will seek Thy name, Lord.
Let them be ashamed and troubled for an age of an age; let them be abashed and perish,

triples.relationship: recognition of the Lord's universal supremacy
triples.rationale: The prayer asks that the opponents know that Thou alone art Lord and glorious over the inhabited world. The psalm similarly asks that they know the Lord alone is Most High over all the earth.
triples.source_text: Let them know that Thou alone art Lord, God, glorious over the whole inhabited world.”

target_units.text: and let them know that Thy name is Lord; Thou alone art Most High over all the earth.

triples.rationale: The description of the furnace's fuel and sevenfold heat returns to the king's command that it be heated seven times beyond what it needed to be heated.
triples.source_text: The king’s servants who threw them in did not stop heating the furnace. When they threw the three together into the furnace, the furnace was sevenfold ablaze in its heat. When they threw them in, those casting them were above them, while others stoked beneath them with naphtha, tow, pitch, and vine brushwood.

target_units.text: Then Nebuchadnezzar was filled with fury, and the appearance of his face changed. He ordered the furnace heated seven times beyond what it needed to be heated.

triples.rationale: The expanded account again describes the fire burning the Chaldeans around the furnace, recalling the earlier report that the flame killed the men who bound the companions while the companions were preserved.
triples.source_text: It spread out and burned those Chaldeans whom it found around the furnace.

target_units.text: The flame came out of the furnace and burned and killed the men who had bound Azariah and his companions; but they themselves were preserved.

triples.rationale: The narrator says the Lord's angel entered with the three men. The king later sees a fourth figure with them and describes that figure as having the likeness of an angel of God.
triples.source_text: An angel of the Lord descended into the furnace together with Azariah and his companions and shook the flame of fire out of the furnace.

target_units.text: “Behold! I see four men unbound, walking in the fire, and no harm has come upon them. The fourth has the likeness of an angel of God.”

triples.rationale: The furnace's interior becomes like a dew-laden breeze, and the fire does not injure the men. Hebrews includes extinguishing the power of fire among the works of faith; this recalls the deliverance motif without explicitly naming the men here.
triples.source_text: He made the middle of the furnace like a dew-laden breeze whistling through. The fire did not touch them at all; it neither distressed nor troubled them.

target_units.text: extinguished the power of fire, escaped the edges of the sword, were strengthened from weakness, became mighty in battle, and turned back the armies of foreigners.

triples.rationale: The three men begin their hymn together in one voice. Within that hymn Hananiah, Azariah and Mishael are explicitly summoned to bless God because He rescued them from the fire.
triples.source_text: Then the three took up the song as with one mouth, singing hymns, glorifying, blessing, and exalting God in the furnace, saying:

target_units.text: Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever. For He rescued us from Hades and saved us from the hand of death; He delivered us from the midst of the burning flame and redeemed us from the fire.

triples.rationale: The hymn blesses the God of the fathers and His enduring glory. David's blessing likewise addresses the Lord, God of Israel and Father, from everlasting to everlasting.
triples.source_text: “Blessed art Thou, Lord, God of our fathers, praised and highly exalted for ever. Blessed is the holy name of Thy glory, exceedingly praised and highly exalted through all ages.

target_units.text: King David blessed the Lord before the assembly, saying, “Blessed art Thou, O Lord, the God of Israel, our Father, from everlasting to everlasting.

triples.rationale: The hymn blesses God in His holy temple. The psalm likewise locates the speaking of glory in His temple, joining the sanctuary with communal praise.
triples.source_text: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy holy glory, exceedingly praised in hymns and exceedingly glorious for ever.

target_units.text: The voice of the Lord, who makes deer ready; and He will uncover forests; in His temple everyone speaks glory.

triples.rationale: The hymn blesses God upon the throne of His kingdom. The psalm declares that the Lord has prepared His throne in heaven and that His kingdom rules over all.
triples.source_text: Blessed art Thou upon the throne of Thy kingdom, praised in hymns and highly exalted for ever.

target_units.text: The Lord prepared His throne in heaven, and His kingdom has dominion over all.

triples.rationale: The hymn addresses God as seated upon the cherubim. The psalm uses the same throne description when asking the shepherd of Israel to appear.
triples.source_text: Blessed art Thou who lookest upon the depths, seated upon cherubim, praised and glorified for ever.

target_units.text: Thou who shepherdest Israel, pay attention, Thou who guidest Joseph like sheep; Thou who sittest upon the cherubim, appear.

triples.rationale: The hymn blesses God in heaven's firmament; the psalm expressly commands praise of Him in the firmament of His power.
triples.source_text: Blessed art Thou in the firmament, praised in hymns and glorified for ever.

target_units.text: Hallelujah. Praise God among His holy ones; praise Him in the firmament of His power.

triples.relationship: shared summons to all God's works
triples.rationale: All the Lord's works are called to bless Him. The psalm similarly calls all His works, in every place of His dominion, to bless the Lord.
triples.source_text: All works of the Lord, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: Bless the Lord, all His works, in every place of His dominion. Bless the Lord, my soul.

triples.rationale: The hymn summons the Lord's angels to bless Him; the psalm summons all His angels to praise Him. The same heavenly company receives the call to worship.
triples.source_text: Angels of the Lord, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: Praise Him, all His angels; praise Him, all His powers.

triples.rationale: The heavens are summoned to bless the Lord. The psalm likewise summons the heavens of heavens to praise Him, giving the heavenly realm a voice in the creation hymn.
triples.source_text: Heavens, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: Praise Him, heavens of heavens, and the water above the heavens.

triples.rationale: Both passages single out the waters above the heavens among those called to praise or bless the Lord, preserving that particular image of creation.
triples.source_text: All waters above heaven, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: Praise Him, heavens of heavens, and the water above the heavens.

triples.rationale: The hymn calls the Lord's powers to bless Him. The psalm similarly calls all His powers and ministers who do His will to bless the Lord.
triples.source_text: All powers of the Lord, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: Bless the Lord, all His powers, His ministers who do His will.

triples.rationale: Sun and moon are addressed together as worshippers of the Lord in both hymns; the shared pair gives the connection its specific content.
triples.source_text: Sun and moon, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: Praise Him, sun and moon; praise Him, all the stars and the light.

triples.rationale: The stars of heaven are called to bless the Lord; the psalm likewise calls all the stars and light to praise Him.
triples.source_text: Stars of heaven, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: Praise Him, sun and moon; praise Him, all the stars and the light.

triples.relationship: praise of God's provision through rain
triples.rationale: The hymn summons rain and dew to bless the Lord. The psalm calls for thanksgiving to God who covers heaven with clouds and prepares rain for the earth, relating rainfall to His praise.
triples.source_text: All rain and dew, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: Begin singing to the Lord with thanksgiving; make music to our God with a lyre,
who clothes heaven with clouds, who prepares rain for the earth, who makes grass sprout on the mountains and green growth for the service of humans,

triples.rationale: The winds are called to bless the Lord. The psalm includes storm wind among the created forces fulfilling His word within its summons to praise.
triples.source_text: All winds, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: fire, hail, snow, ice, storm wind—all fulfilling His word,

triples.rationale: Fire and heat are summoned to bless God even within the furnace song. The psalm also includes fire among the created forces that fulfill His word and praise Him.
triples.source_text: Fire and heat, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: fire, hail, snow, ice, storm wind—all fulfilling His word,

triples.rationale: The hymn calls chill and cold to bless God. The psalm attributes ice and cold to Him, asks who can withstand His cold, and says His word melts the ice, placing these conditions under His authority.
triples.source_text: Chill and cold, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: who casts His ice like morsels; who will withstand His cold?
He will send His word and melt them; He will blow His wind, and waters will flow.

triples.relationship: praise of the maker of snow
triples.rationale: The hymn includes snow with dew in its summons to bless God. The psalm praises God's giving of snow and ice and His word that melts them; snow is the particular shared element.
triples.source_text: Dews and snowfalls, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: of Him who gives snow like wool, who sprinkles mist like ashes,
who casts His ice like morsels; who will withstand His cold?
He will send His word and melt them; He will blow His wind, and waters will flow.

triples.relationship: divine authority over ice and cold
triples.rationale: Ice and cold are summoned to bless the Lord; the psalm names both as God's works and describes the ice melting at His word.
triples.source_text: Ice and cold, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: who casts His ice like morsels; who will withstand His cold?
He will send His word and melt them; He will blow His wind, and waters will flow.

triples.rationale: The hymn addresses hoarfrost and snow. The psalm likewise places snow and ice within creation's praise, describing these wintry elements as fulfilling God's word.
triples.source_text: Hoarfrost and snow, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: fire, hail, snow, ice, storm wind—all fulfilling His word,

triples.rationale: The hymn summons nights and days to bless the Lord; the psalm explicitly declares that both day and night belong to Him. Both retain the paired ordering of time under God.
triples.source_text: Nights and days, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: Thine is the day, and Thine is the night; Thou didst fashion light and the sun.

triples.rationale: Light and darkness are called to bless God. Genesis describes God bringing light into being, distinguishing it from darkness and naming the two; the hymn addresses that ordered pair within creation.
triples.source_text: Light and darkness, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: And God said, “Let there be light.” And there was light.
And God saw that the light was good, and God divided the light from the darkness.
And God called the light Day, and the darkness He called Night. And there was evening, and there was morning: one day.

triples.relationship: praise of the maker of clouds and lightning
triples.rationale: Lightning and clouds are addressed in the hymn. The psalm likewise attributes the rising of clouds and the making of lightning for rain to the Lord, naming the same atmospheric works.
triples.source_text: Lightning and clouds, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: He brings clouds up from the earth’s extremity; He made lightning for rain; He brings winds out of His treasuries.

triples.rationale: The earth is called to bless the Lord. The psalm likewise commands praise of the Lord from the earth before enumerating its creatures and forces.
triples.source_text: Let the earth bless the Lord; let her sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: Praise the Lord from the earth, dragons and all deeps,

triples.rationale: Both hymns summon mountains and hills together into the praise of God, retaining the same paired features of the land.
triples.source_text: Mountains and hills, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: mountains and all hills, fruit-bearing trees and all cedars,

triples.rationale: The hymn addresses growing plants of the earth; the psalm specifically includes fruit-bearing trees and cedars among creation's worshippers. Those named trees belong to the plant life addressed by the hymn.
triples.source_text: All things growing upon the earth, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: mountains and all hills, fruit-bearing trees and all cedars,

triples.relationship: praise of God's provision through springs
triples.rationale: Springs are summoned to bless the Lord. The psalm describes His sending springs into ravines to supply the animals' thirst, identifying their place in His care of creation.
triples.source_text: Springs, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: He sends springs into the ravines; waters will pass between the mountains.
They give drink to all the beasts of the field; wild donkeys will receive it for their thirst.

triples.rationale: The hymn addresses seas and rivers together. The psalm similarly calls the sea to be stirred and rivers to clap their hands, personifying these waters in joyful response to God.
triples.source_text: Seas and rivers, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: Let the sea be shaken, and all that fills it, the inhabited world and those who dwell in it.
Rivers will clap their hands together; the mountains will exult,

triples.relationship: liturgical parallel of creatures and depths
triples.rationale: The hymn calls sea monsters and creatures moving in water to bless God. The psalm's corresponding summons names dragons and the deeps, bringing great creatures and deep waters into creation's praise.
triples.source_text: Sea monsters and all things moving in the waters, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: Praise the Lord from the earth, dragons and all deeps,

triples.rationale: The hymn calls the birds of heaven to bless the Lord; the psalm includes winged birds among the creatures called to praise Him.
triples.source_text: All birds of heaven, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: wild animals and all cattle, creeping things and winged birds,

triples.rationale: Quadrupeds and wild animals are addressed together in the hymn. The psalm likewise calls wild animals and specifically cattle into creation's praise, overlapping the hymn's stated land-animal groups.
triples.source_text: Four-footed creatures and wild animals of the earth, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: wild animals and all cattle, creeping things and winged birds,

triples.rationale: The hymn calls humankind to bless God. The psalm expands that human company into peoples, rulers, men, women, old and young, all summoned to praise the Lord.
triples.source_text: Sons of humankind, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: kings of the earth and all peoples, rulers and all judges of the earth,
young men and young women, old people with younger people.

triples.rationale: Israel is explicitly called to bless the Lord in the hymn; the psalm issues the same call to the house of Israel.
triples.source_text: Israel, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: House of Israel, bless the Lord; house of Aaron, bless the Lord.

triples.rationale: The hymn summons the Lord's priests to bless Him; the psalm calls the house of Aaron to bless Him. Exodus 28:1 explicitly appoints Aaron and his sons to priestly service, establishing the priestly household addressed by the psalm.
triples.source_text: Priests, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: House of Israel, bless the Lord; house of Aaron, bless the Lord.

triples.rationale: The hymn calls the Lord's servants to bless Him. The psalm likewise addresses all the Lord's slaves standing in His house and commands them to bless Him.
triples.source_text: Servants, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: A song of the ascents. Behold, bless the Lord, all slaves of the Lord, who stand in the Lord’s house, in the courts of the house of our God.

triples.relationship: shared description of the worshipping company
triples.rationale: The hymn includes the spirits and souls of righteous people among those blessing God. Hebrews describes the heavenly assembly as including the spirits of righteous ones made perfect, alongside angels and the assembly before God.
triples.source_text: Spirits and souls of the righteous, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: But you have approached Mount Zion and the city of the living God, heavenly Jerusalem, and myriads of angels in festive gathering,
and the assembly of firstborn ones enrolled in the heavens, and God the judge of all, and the spirits of righteous ones who have been perfected,

triples.rationale: The hymn summons holy people and the humble in heart to bless God. The psalm likewise calls the meek to hear and rejoice and invites them to magnify the Lord together.
triples.source_text: Holy ones and those humble in heart, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever.

target_units.text: My soul will be praised in the Lord; let the meek hear and rejoice.
Magnify the Lord with me; let us exalt His name together.

triples.rationale: The named companions thank God for rescue from death and the furnace. Their earlier answer had trusted His rescue and maintained their refusal to worship the king's idol.
triples.source_text: Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael, bless the Lord; sing praise to Him and exalt Him highly for ever. For He rescued us from Hades and saved us from the hand of death; He delivered us from the midst of the burning flame and redeemed us from the fire.

target_units.text: For there is a God in the heavens, our one Lord, whom we fear, who is able to rescue us from the furnace of fire; and from your hands, O king, He will rescue us.
Then it will be plain to you that we neither serve your idol nor bow to your golden image that you set up.”

triples.rationale: Both passages call for thanksgiving to the Lord because He is good or kind and His mercy is forever, joining the summons with the same enduring-mercy refrain.
triples.source_text: Give thanks to the Lord, for He is good, for His mercy endures for ever.
